Simple banh cuon
Jul 2017
Simple banh cuon, but lack of herbs. A plate of banh cuon contains two rolls of banh cuon, shredded lettuce and steamed sprouts. Unfortunately, no herbs!!! So disappointed. So I knocked off a star. Otherwise, this place wholeheartedly deserves 5 stars. The rice flour wrapping was soft, thin and slightly chewy. Perfect. The fillings contained pork, wood ear fungus (sounds gross, but they bring out the crunchiness that works perfectly well with any meat filling), dried shrimp and ground peppercorns. It also served with two pork patties on the side. We ordered cha Giò (egg rolls) also. The rolls were pretty big with generous fillings. Perfectly seasoned. Comparable to the one in Quan Nem these cha Giò taste the same, only slightly less crunchy than Quan Nem's. 

Tips: afterward, walk across the street to your right, a few stores down is "HEBE Tea and Coffee"!! Best coffee and tea!

Marquee Vietnamese snack served in a humble-sized restaurant
Jul 2015 • Solo
For the uninitiated, Banh Cuon is basically minced pork wrapped in paper-thin steamed noddle wrappers, peppered with fried shrimp and typically dunked in fish and chilli sauce. 

Preparing the wrapper requires a great deal of finesse-- a process which is done right at the entrance.

Banh Cuon is their speciality here and the dish is accompanied with gigantic portion of bean sprouts and shredded lettuce. All these for just about a dollar! 

The restaurant is definitely small for its popularity and hence there is little wonder that it is packed with locals (the best form of quality assurance to me). I shared my table with 2 other grateful locals.

This dish makes for a fine snack/appetizer as I proceed to wolf down a delicious bowl of pho just couple of streets down.

Saigon's best Bánh Cuốn
Oct 2013 • Friends
I have lived in Saigon for 12 years and this is absolutely the best banh cuon in the city. The dish is rice paper rolled with pork and shrimp and covered with bean sprouts. Scoop out fish sauce from the jar on the table, add a dollop or two of chili, and pour over the rolls. The side dishes not to miss are the chả (something like baloney but silky smooth and delicious) and bánh tôm (shrimp cakes). Wash it down with a glass of fresh soy milk and you just had the best and healthiest $2 meal of your life. Don't expect fancy surroundings at that price, but the place is relatively clean and hygienic by Vietnamese standards and oozes local charm.

Truely Authentic Vietnamese Flavours
Aug 2013 • Couples
Firstly, the location that tripadvisor shoes is completely wrong. This restaurant is located at 11a Cao Thang, but it's the Cao Thang street at the end of Cong Quynh. About 500m walk from the main Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district.

Ok, so onto the actual review. We were recommended this place by our hotel manager. This food is authentic. Flavours in Pham Ngu Lao are diluted and usually disappointing. A short walk and you can get all that makes Vietnamese food fantastic.

The banh cuon dish is prepared fresh upon ordering. Two rolls, with lettuce and mung bean for 28,000 VND. Sooo cheap and sooo delicious. 

If you don't know what banh cuon is, it's minced meat rolled in a thin steamed soft rice flour. Kind of like a giant filled rice noodle. Anyway, this is worth trying during your stay.

Service is very friendly and they have an english menu.
